lesion: Anterior cruciate ligament tear with surgery
contexto: 24-year-old player, non-contact injury during a change of direction. Stated goal: returning to competition at the same level.
intervencion: Restoring full extension and neuromuscular control before maximal strength
Load progression driven by the gap between the healthy and operated leg, reviewed every three weeks
Running reintroduced only after reaching 80 % strength symmetry
Final eight weeks devoted to competition actions under accumulated fatigue
resultado: Full clearance at 34 weeks with 96 % strength symmetry. A complete season afterwards, with no re-injury.

contexto: Second injury in the same area within a year, in a player with little previous strength training.
intervencion: Eccentric work from week one, progressing through range of motion
Correction of the posterior-chain strength deficit, which was the real origin
Clearance conditional on matching the healthy side and completing two full training sessions
resultado: Return at six weeks, followed by a season and a half without any further injury in that area.

contexto: Player with a history of instability and clear apprehension when landing from jumps.
intervencion: Restoring single-leg loading with progressive load before returning to jumping
Specific landing and deceleration work on different surfaces
Gradual exposure to the situations causing apprehension, tracked on video
resultado: Return to competition in nine weeks, with no instability episodes over the following two years.

contexto: Progressive pain over months in the striking arm, with no possible break mid-season.
intervencion: Reduced striking volume without withdrawing from competition, agreed with the player
Shoulder and scapular strength programme three days a week
Daily pain scale monitoring to adjust load week by week
resultado: Pain below the acceptable threshold at fourteen weeks, without missing a single official match.
